Speakers.title: Check the speakers from the 2025 edition
Speakers.subtitle: Look at these amazing human beings

serena.name: Serena Sensini
serena.talk: Large Language Models have led the charge in the generative AI landscape, particularly following the introduction of tools such as ChatGPT or Perplexity. Despite this progress, their full capabilities remain untapped, primarily due to cost-related challenges. This talk will delve into the often-overlooked financial aspects of incorporating AI into organizational structures, and the potential of open source models to achieve transparency and awareness. Although AI technologies are touted for their potential to boost efficiency and productivity, the expenses tied to their implementation can be significant and complex.

claire.name: Claire Fletcher Harris
claire.job_title: Site Reliability Engineer @Kaluza & WG Sustainability Advocacy Chair
claire.talk_title: From shy contributor to (kinda) confident community leader
claire.talk:
At least once in the life of a software engineer or someone who works in technology, you will hear that contributing to open source is important and that you should try it. For some people, however, contributing doesn't just mean fixing a bug or updating some documentation. For these people, it means finding the right community to proudly be a part of, fighting their shyness, and then developing the confidence to jump in.
In this talk, Claire & Valeria will share their personal experiences as people who started off as contributors and then became community leaders. They will share some tips for getting started, how you can take the next step and then, eventually, become an ambassador for your community.

valeria.name: Valeria Salis
valeria.talk_title: From shy contributor to (kinda) confident community leader
valeria.talk:
At least once in the life of a software engineer or someone who works in technology, you will hear that contributing to open source is important and that you should try it. For some people, however, contributing doesn't just mean fixing a bug or updating some documentation. For these people, it means finding the right community to proudly be a part of, fighting their shyness, and then developing the confidence to jump in.
In this talk, Claire & Valeria will share their personal experiences as people who started off as contributors and then became community leaders. They will share some tips for getting started, how you can take the next step and then, eventually, become an ambassador for your community.

cosmin.name: Cosmin Marian Paduraru
cosmin.talk_title: Unlocking Visual Intelligence | Exploring Computer Vision with Python
cosmin.talk:
Join me on a thrilling exploration of computer vision with Python. I've crafted solutions like a bottle cap detection app and boardgames cover identification, employing techniques such as SIFT and Hough Transform Circles. Let's delve into image processing, uncovering the secrets to building intelligent visual recognition systems together.

Despite not working directly in computer vision roles, my passion for the field has been unwavering. I've dedicated my spare time to exploring its possibilities, diving into additional projects and even tackling assignments during my university years.

edoardo.name: Edoardo Calesi
edoardo.job_title: Theoretical physicist, machine learning specialist, Nanowar Of Steel bass & management
edoardo.talk_title: The Universe, The (Hello) World and Uranus
edoardo.talk: In this talk I will focus on my work in science and technology: First, as an astrophysicist in the field of computational cosmology and then as a Machine Learning specialist working on Earth Observations. I will talk about my projects in these fields, and how my scientific and IT background is intertwined with my parallel music career with Nanowar Of Steel, inspiring songs like Uranus and the recent internet sensation HelloWorld.java

matteo.name: Matteo Valentini
matteo.talk_title: Make or Buy is the new Fight or Flight: The Survival Journey of NethServer in a Fast-Paced World
matteo.talk:
What happens when a successful classic Linux distribution, supported by a well-established international community of users and backed by a company, faces the challenges of a fast-paced open-source world of cloud-native technologies, containers, and Kubernetes?
Will the project abandon its roots and embrace new trends (Buy/Flight)?
Or will it stick to its original mission and values (Make/Fight)?

giorgio.name: Giorgio Boa
giorgio.talk_title: Open Source: The Ultimate Code Career Accelerator
giorgio.talk:
Forget traditional resumes - let your open source contributions tell your story!
My open source evolution from contributor to maintainer shows how community involvement supercharges your dev skills and leadership potential. Through real experiences, I'll demonstrate how engaging with open source projects builds your professional reputation and opens career doors, while learning directly from industry experts.
Let me show you how open source collaboration can transform your development journey and unlock your true potential!

leonardo.name: Leonardo Cavagnis
leonardo.talk_title: Scaling IoT Development with Zephyr: An Embedded System OS for the Future
leonardo.talk: An embedded system is a specialized computer designed to perform specific tasks. Some embedded systems run without an OS, while others use an OS to enable advanced functionality such as multitasking, networking, real-time processing, and more - essential for complex IoT applications.

pierdomenico.name: Pierdomenico Reitano
pierdomenico.job_title: Front End Developer | firenze.dev core member
pierdomenico.talk_title: Dungeons And Developers: Epic Teamwork for Legendary Projects
pierdomenico.talk:
What if your tech team was a party of adventurers, and every sprint was an epic quest? Dungeons & Developers reimagines software development through the lens of fantasy role-playing games like Dungeons & Dragons. This humorous and engaging talk explores how creating character sheets for team members—highlighting their strengths, weaknesses, and “special abilities”—can foster deeper understanding, collaboration, and trust within your team.
With a lighthearted approach, we’ll also dive into how this creative framework can inspire open-source projects and team-building methodologies that gamify workflows. Whether it’s a fantasy-themed sprint planner or a role-playing retrospective, you’ll leave with practical tools, a good laugh, and fresh ideas to make teamwork fun and effective.

marco.name: Marco Ippolito
marco.talk:
Imagine the convenience of executing TypeScript files directly with Node.js using `node file.ts`. Just a few years ago, this concept seemed like a distant dream. Today, it stands as an exciting experimental feature. This narrative dives into the journey of transforming this dream into a reality.
Integrating TypeScript natively into Node.js posed significant challenges. These hurdles included managing TypeScript’s lack of strict semantic versioning guarantees and accommodating various TS flavors.
Today, the experimental native TypeScript support in Node.js marks a transformative milestone. Beyond merely executing .ts files, it signifies a leap forward in JavaScript development.

stefano.name: Stefano Marinelli
stefano.job_title: Owner and tech at Prodottoinrete Group SRL, Founder of the BSD Cafe
stefano.talk_title: Why Choose to Use the BSDs in 2025
stefano.talk: In a world increasingly dominated by buzzwords and trends, terms like "cloud," "serverless," "Kubernetes," and Linux are on everyone's lips. So why move away from the now most common solutions and adopt those based on one of the operating systems in the BSD family?In computing, the goal is to solve problems. And the BSDs, in the vast majority of cases, can be excellent tools to address these challenges while also mitigating the widespread issue of IT monoculture and its related consequences.A brief introduction and analysis of the BSD family operating systems and their unique characteristics.

emiliano.name: Emiliano Pisu
emiliano.talk_title: wcagUI, an accessible UI kit based on WCAG patterns
emiliano.talk:
Building an accessible web experience shouldn’t be overwhelming. In this talk, we’ll introduce wcagUI, an open-source UI kit that simplifies building accessible interfaces by automatically handling WAI-ARIA attributes and other key accessibility features. Built on the principles of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), wcagUI helps developers and designers integrate accessibility seamlessly into their projects, reducing complexity and allowing a focus on great user experiences.
With a zero-dependencies philosophy and no view encapsulation, wcagUI is lightweight, transparent, and compatible with any tech stack. Developed using modern JavaScript and the customElements API, its reusable components manage accessibility features like WAI-ARIA roles and states automatically. wcagUI also adheres to progressive enhancement principles, ensuring components provide core functionality even when JavaScript is unavailable, making interfaces more resilient and inclusive.
As the European Accessibility Act (EAA) enforces strict accessibility requirements across the EU, tools like wcagUI are more critical than ever. By streamlining compliance and making accessibility effortless, wcagUI not only ensures inclusivity but also helps avoid legal risks and keeps your products competitive. This talk will equip you with the knowledge and tools to create accessible, future-ready projects with confidence.

maciek.name: Maciek Palmowski
maciek.talk_title: How we closed almost 1000 plugins in a month - a story of the biggest WordPress bug bounty hunt
maciek.talk:
In October 2024, our usual bug bounty hunt resulted in receiving 1570 valid reports and closing almost 1000 plugins from the official WordPress repository. This huge number looks scary and seems once again to prove the fact that WordPress ecosystem security is poor.
But is it?
Let's dive deeper into how it all happened, what were the consequences, and what we can learn from this.

sal.name: Sal Kimmich
sal.talk_title: Bridging Law and Technology: The Foundations and Future of Computational Justice
sal.talk:
Open source is driving innovation at the intersection of law and technology, enabling the creation of systems that are transparent, secure, and accountable. This session will examine how open-source frameworks and confidential computing solutions are shaping the future of computational justice and reinforcing digital sovereignty. 
Key topics include how Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) and Remote Attestation are enabling verifiable compute, and how cryptographic techniques like Multi-Party Computation and Zero-Knowledge Proofs ensure privacy without sacrificing accountability. We'll also explore how these technologies empower organisations to maintain control over their data, ensuring compliance with data residency and sovereignty requirements. For instance, confidential computing allows data to be processed securely within specific jurisdictions, preventing unauthorised access and aligning with regional regulations.
Using examples from 2024, such as AI-assisted evidence handling and fair algorithmic decision-making, we will illustrate the transformative role of open-source projects in enhancing trust in the legal domain and supporting sovereign data governance. This talk is perfect for developers, legal tech innovators, and open-source advocates seeking to understand how collaborative technologies can advance justice while upholding the principles of digital sovereignty.

Venue.subtitle: L'événement est organisé par Nana Bianca, au cœur de Florence
Venue.heading: ARRIVÉE SUR LE LIEU DE L'ÉVÉNEMENT
Venue.train_infos: De la gare centrale de Firenze SMN, vous pouvez rejoindre le lieu à pied (15min.), ou prendre un bus (lignes C4/6 arrêt : Soderini Torrino Santa Rosa).
Venue.plane_infos_1: De l'aéroport de Florence : prendre le tramway, ligne T2, arrêt : Alamanni - Stazione Santa Maria Novella
Venue.plane_infos_2: Depuis l'aéroport de Pise : Prenez le PisaMover depuis l'aéroport jusqu'à Pise Centrale. Le Pisamover vous permet de rejoindre l'aéroport avec un service de navette en moins de 3 minutes. La navette fonctionne de 6h00 à minuit. Prenez ensuite un <link_train>train</link_train> pour Firenze Santa Maria Novella (1h/1h30m).
Venue.plane_infos_3: Depuis l'aéroport de Bologne : un <link_minibus>minibus</link_minibus> peut vous conduire à la gare de Bologne Centrale. Vous pouvez ensuite choisir de rejoindre Florence en <link_bus>bus</link_bus> (1h30) ou en <link_train>train</link_train>. Vous ne devriez pas choisir la solution train 1h+ sauf si vous voulez voir toutes les gares entre bologne et florence (30min. avec Frecciarossa ou 1h avec le train régional). Il y a aussi une autre compagnie <link_italo>train</link_italo> qui fait cet itinéraire.
Venue.car_infos: Voici une liste de <link>parking payant</link>. Les plus proches du lieu de réunion sont : Porta al Prato - Leopolda, Stazione S.M.N et S. Lorenzo - Mercato Centrale

Faq.faq_answer_0: L'after party est organisée à 18h30 dans le bar situé dans l'enceinte de l'événement. Les places sont limitées aux seuls participants présents. Malheureusement, nous avons estimé le nombre de personnes en tenant compte d'un éventuel retrait de billets le jour de l'événement. En entrant dans la salle, vous obtiendrez donc un document à présenter au personnel pour obtenir des boissons. En cas de dépassement du nombre de participants, nous ne pourrons malheureusement pas offrir plus, mais nous espérons que vous pourrez tout de même profiter de cette opportunité de réseautage.
Faq.faq_answer_1: Bien sûr ! Vous pouvez entrer quand vous le souhaitez. Un membre du personnel sera présent à l'entrée pour vérifier les billets et vous remettre le badge.
Faq.faq_answer_2: Nous proposons de la nourriture uniquement pendant l'after party, en guise d'apéritif. Nous avons organisé un prix réduit avec le lieu, tant pour le lancement que pour les pauses café. Vous pouvez acheter votre propre nourriture au <link_stellar>The Stellar</link_stellar>.
Faq.faq_answer_3: L'événement sera retransmis sur YouTube pour les deux jours et les deux pistes. Vous pouvez visionner les enregistrements quand vous le souhaitez. De plus, toutes les conférences seront téléchargées séparément quelques jours après l'événement.
Faq.faq_answer_4: Non, seul le billet est nécessaire.
Faq.faq_answer_5: Oui, l'ordre du jour est disponible sur le site de la conférence ! Aller à l'<link_agenda>agenda</link_agenda>

CodeOfConduct.title: Open Source Day 2025
CodeOfConduct.subtitle: Code de conduite
CodeOfConduct.shortVersion_text: Schrödinger Hat is dedicated to a harassment-free event for everyone.
CodeOfConduct.longVersion_text: Schrödinger Hat is dedicated to providing a harassment-free event experience for everyone, regardless of gender, gender identity and expression, age, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion (or lack thereof), or technology choices. We do not tolerate harassment of event participants in any form. Sexual language and imagery is not appropriate for any event venue, including talks, workshops, parties, Twitter and other online media. Event participants violating these rules may be sanctioned or expelled from the event without a refund at the discretion of the Schrödinger Hat organisers.
CodeOfConduct.completeVersion_text: Schrödinger Hat is dedicated to providing a harassment-free event experience for everyone. Harassment includes, but is not limited to: Offensive verbal comments related to gender, gender identity and expression, age, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion, technology choices. Sexual language and images in public spaces. Deliberate intimidation, threats, stalking or following. Harassing photography or recording. Sustained disruption of talks or other events. Inappropriate physical contact. Unwelcome sexual attention. Advocating for, or encouraging, any of the above behaviour Sponsors, speakers, recruiters and organisers should not use sexualised images, activities, or other material. All staff and organisers related to the event (Schrödinger Hat organisers, venue staff and sponsor's staff - including volunteers) should not use sexualised clothing/uniforms/costumes, or otherwise create a sexualised environment. Schrödinger Hat organisers may also provide an additional code of conduct for the needs of individual communication channels or events.
CodeOfConduct.enforcement_text: Anyone asked to stop any harassing behavior are expected to comply immediately. If anyone engages in harassing behavior, the Schrödinger Hat organisers may take any action they deem appropriate, including warning the offender or expulsion from the event with no refund. This applies to all Schrödinger Hat events and associated communication channels. Everyone using Schrödinger Hat services or attending Schrödinger Hat events is subject to the anti-harassment policy; this includes attendees, sponsors, speakers, recruiters and organisers.
CodeOfConduct.reporting_text: If you are being harassed, notice that someone else is being harassed, or have any other concerns, please contact a member of Schrödinger Hat staff immediately. You can make a personal report by: Twitter's direct message service: @schrodinger_hat. Email: social@schroedinger-hat.org Phone (organiser's numbers are shared at the beginning of the event and monitored during the event). Reaching out to an organiser who will make sure the conversation is held privately. You will not be asked to confront anyone and we won't tell anyone who you are. We will identify ourselves at the beginning of each event. Schrödinger Hat staff will be happy to help participants contact venue security (if available) or local law enforcement, provide escorts, or otherwise assist those experiencing harassment to feel safe for the duration of the event. We value your attendance. We expect everyone to follow these rules at the all the events organised by Schrödinger Hat (meetups, workshops, other events and post meetup related social events).
